page: Vultr vx1-m-2c-16g is an x86_64 virtual server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz, configured as 1 physical core with 2 threads. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is limited to a 1 GB network-attached volume, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. There are no onboard GPUs.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance alongside constrained multi-core capabilities. The server achieves top-tier results in single-core stress-ng tests, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression. However, multi-core CPU performance and PassMark CPU scores fall into the bottom tier, reflecting the physical single-core limitation. Memory bandwidth is average for large block reads and writes but weak for small block cached reads. Database operations, Redis SET performance, and LLM inference tasks generally rank in the lower tier, though static web serving throughput remains average at 7.66 GB/sec.

From a resource density perspective, this instance offers a cost-efficient profile for workloads requiring a larger memory footprint without demanding high multi-core compute power. The primary tradeoff is the single physical core architecture, which limits parallel processing capacity and multi-threaded execution speeds. Additionally, the minimal 1 GB network storage requires external storage solutions for data-intensive applications.

This server is best suited for memory-intensive but computationally light workloads. Appropriate use cases include single-threaded application servers, lightweight caching layers, static web serving, and basic memory-optimized utility tasks that do not require high-speed local disk I/O or multi-core scaling.
